1. Reading the Table

The table lists 137 guns by class. Each group's first row gives its class,
level, eligibility for surveying and printing, and number of models.
Models within each group are ordered by value, lowest first.

"Value" is the base value in the tooltip. The six stats are for Good
condition with no attachments. The headers "Rel.", "Recoil", "Ergo." and
"Acc." mean Reliability, Recoil Control, Ergonomics and Accuracy,
respectively.
2. Repairability

Repairability determines the success chance when refurbishing a gun
with Gun Parts. It is not shown in the tooltip. Drag Gun Parts owned by
the store onto a gun in Poor, Fair or Good condition to see the current
success chance. The gun must belong to the store or have been handed
over by a customer for a repair or modification order.

The first attempt's success chance equals repairability. Each failure adds
that amount to the next attempt's chance. A Journeyman, Senior or
Master Repair Certificate in the store adds 5, 10 or 15 percentage points,
respectively, to every attempt. The maximum chance is 100%.

Each refurbishment attempt consumes one unit of Gun Parts. Success
improves condition by one grade and resets the next attempt's chance to
repairability.

Example: Rampart Heavy Machine Gun has repairability 25. Without a
certificate bonus, successive success chances are 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%.
With a Master Repair Certificate in the store, they are 40%, 65%, 90%,
100%.

A gun with known unrepaired or emergency-repaired faults cannot be
refurbished. Dragging Gun Parts onto it shows red highlighting; releasing
returns the Gun Parts. Undiscovered faults do not affect refurbishment.

1. Attachment Bonuses

With attachments fitted, a gun's current stat = base stat × (100 +
condition bonus + sum of fitted attachment percentage
bonuses) ÷ 100, discarding the fractional part, then adding the
sum of fitted attachment flat bonuses. See Chapter 5 for
condition bonuses.

Example: a Raven Type B Pistol in Good condition has 45 Accuracy. With
a Closedwindow Red Dot (Accuracy +7, +23%), calculate 45 × 123 ÷ 100
and discard the fractional part to get 55. Add 7 for a total of 62.

1. Classes and Levels
Class
Guns fall into 16 classes; see Chapter 1. Class is not shown in the tooltip.
Level

Gun levels match contraband levels, from 1 to 4 (Chapter 1). For levels
brought by visitors or requested in orders, see Chapters 2 and 7 of
"Gunsmithing Manual".
Contraband and Restricted Goods

Level 1 to 4 firearms and ammunition are contraband, labeled Low-Level,
Mid-Level, High-Level or Critical-Level Contraband in the tooltip, with a
[Contraband] tag. The store's Class I, Class II and Class III Weapon Permits
make Level 1, 2 and 3 firearms and ammunition restricted goods tagged
[Restricted I], [Restricted II] and [Restricted III], respectively. Level 4 has
no permit. Gun and pistol frames share their gun's level.

When customers buy the store's contraband, the level adds +35%, +70%,
+100% or +150% to the price. Restricted goods add +17%, +35% or +50%,
respectively.
2. Stats and Condition
Stats

Guns have six stats: Firepower, Style, Reliability, Recoil Control,
Ergonomics and Accuracy. Current values depend on base values,
condition and attachments. See Chapter 3 for the calculation.

Stats matter only for orders. Customers set stat requirements, which are
met when the delivered gun's current values reach the required values.

Custom orders, gun modification orders, long-term contracts, collectors
and "best in class" orders set stat requirements (Chapter 7 of
"Gunsmithing Manual").
Condition

Guns have five condition grades. Condition modifies both value and all
six stats:

Guns printed by a 3D Printer are New, as are guns assembled from
printed gun or pistol frames. For guns that have had faults, condition
depends on those faults. Any undiscovered or unrepaired fault gives Poor
condition and the modifier "Unrepaired faults" -45%. If all faults have
received repairs but any repair is an emergency repair, condition is Fair.
Full repairs throughout give Good condition, or Excellent with a Master
Repair Certificate in the store.
Repairability

Repairability is a value assigned to each model that
determines the success chance of refurbishment with Gun
Parts. It is not shown in the tooltip. See Chapter 2 for
refurbishment rules and each model's value.
3. Attachments and Faults
Attachment Slots

The attachment window has up to 8 slots: Stock, Rail, Barrel, Magazine,
Underbarrel, Special 1, Special 2 and Special 3. Some guns show only a
subset. See Chapter 3 for each gun's compatible attachments.
Faults

Guns can have six fault types: Loose or missing screws,
Wiring fault, Rust and fouling (surface, examined with a
Magnifying Glass); Worn parts, Cracked weld, Bent barrel
(internal, examined with a Portable XRay Scanner). Old
and antique guns have no Wiring fault.

Fault statuses: "needs repair", "emergency repair", "repaired".
Undiscovered faults are absent from the tooltip. For inspection and
repairs, see "Gunsmithing Manual", Chapter 3.
4. Chips and Surveying
3D Printer Chips

A 3D Printer Chip in a 3D Printer prints its corresponding item. Each gun
eligible for surveying and printing has its own chip; Farshore Light Pistol
3D Printer Chip, for example, prints a Farshore Light Pistol Frame. Drag
one unit of Gun Parts onto a gun or pistol frame to assemble the gun. Chip
materials, values and sources are in Chapters 5 and 6 of "Gunsmithing
Manual".
Blank 3D Printer Chips and Surveying

Blank 3D Printer Chips come in Restricted I, Restricted II and Restricted
III.

To survey a gun, drag a Blank 3D Printer Chip onto a gun of the same
level owned by the store to obtain its 3D Printer Chip. The gun remains.
Level 1 requires a Magnifying Glass in the store; Levels 2 and 3 require a
Portable XRay Scanner. With the wrong chip level or a missing tool,
surveying is unavailable: the gun highlights red during dragging, and the
chip returns on release.

Survey eligibility is listed by class in Chapter 1. Critical contraband
classes and Old and antique guns cannot be surveyed.
